bounds: SentenceBoundary
A startup’s financials help you understand what it has earned, spent, and still owes.
SentenceBoundary
Revenue is not the same as profit, and cash on hand is not the same as available runway.
SentenceBoundary
Burn rate describes cash being used over time.
SentenceBoundary
Gross burn looks at cash operating outflows; net burn subtracts cash inflows such as receipts.
SentenceBoundary
Runway is a rough estimate of how long current cash might last at the current net burn.
SentenceBoundary
In a fictional example, a company has $180,000 in cash, spends $60,000 each month, and collects $30,000 in monthly receipts.
SentenceBoundary
Its net burn is $30,000 per month, so simple runway is six months.
SentenceBoundary
That assumes the pace stays constant and ignores timing, debt, and one-time expenses.
SentenceBoundary
Check the period covered by statements, unpaid bills, customer concentration, and planned use of proceeds.
SentenceBoundary
A runway estimate is a snapshot, not a promise that the company will raise more money or survive until the date shown.
